neighbours.label: the preposition 'de' / 'di' / 'of' linking a noun to a following noun or name (noun-de-noun), strongest in French, Italian and Spanish
fire: Nous avons visité le château de Versailles pendant les vacances.
Elle a trouvé une vieille photo de famille dans le grenier.
Abbiamo comprato una bottiglia di vino rosso per la cena.
Il professore di storia ha parlato per due ore.
El libro de recetas estaba encima de la mesa.
Hemos alquilado una casa de campo cerca del lago.
It was the longest day of summer and nobody wanted to go home.
The mayor gave a short speech in front of the cathedral of Chartres.
quiet: Nous avons visité le château avec nos cousins pendant les vacances.
Elle a trouvé une vieille photo jaunie dans le grenier.
Abbiamo comprato una bottiglia grande per la cena.
Il professore anziano ha parlato per due ore.
El libro nuevo estaba encima de la mesa.
Hemos alquilado una casa pequeña cerca del lago.
It was the longest summer day and nobody wanted to go home.
The mayor gave a short speech in front of the old cathedral.

notes: card: ' de' dominates the top 32 (x17), also ' at', ' of', ' di'. Probes uneven: 'livre de Marie' 0.43, 'museo di Roma' 0.33, 'best night of the trip' 0.26, 'casa de mi' 0.15, 'precio de la' 0.01. Near misses: the same sentences with the linking preposition replaced by another word.
